links.note: Assertion-reason on Mrs Shaw advising Mary to laugh a lot and make the guests laugh. This is Mrs Shaw's coaching before the visit, which 28272 covers.
Assertion-reason on Mrs Shaw telling Mary not to look glad when the guests are ready to leave - again Mrs Shaw's instructions to Mary.
Who Mrs Harding's husband was - Mr Harding, a wealthy man. Establishes the guests Mrs Shaw is tidying the room for.
Where the Hardings lived before Lanfield - London. Background of the expected guests, part of the visit 28272 opens.
Mrs Lee's relation to Mr Harding - his sister. Identifies the second guest Mrs Shaw is preparing for.
What Mary's mother wanted her to be to people - kind. Mrs Shaw's instruction, not Mary's failure to follow it (28275).
What Mary should do if everyone stopped talking - say something to make them talk again. Mrs Shaw's rule for the visit.
Assertion-reason: Mary makes several blunders, but the claim that she consistently applies her mother's advice is false. Tests whether her remarks were polite.
Assertion-reason on Mrs Lee's banker brother reading newspapers - the exchange in which Mary's 'bankers can't think' lands as an insult.
Mrs Harding's reply, 'Oh, I haven't any children' - the moment Mary's compliment is exposed as an impolite blunder.
What Mary said bankers couldn't do - think. One of the statements on the impolite side of 28275's sort.
How Mrs Harding reacted when Mary claimed to have seen her children - a polite but displeased correction, and an awkward moment.
Mary's insensitive remark about Mrs Cotter staying in bed and seeing the doctor, which Mrs Harding herself does. Impolite talk.
Mary's opinion that bankers can't think, and that she offended Mrs Lee with it. Recognising the remark as impolite.
Mary's comment that the dog looks dirty and that she dislikes dogs - Towzer is Mrs Harding's. A statement that does not display polite behaviour.
Extract in which Mary compliments Mrs Harding's non-existent children and insists she has seen them. The blunder itself, so 28275.
Diary entry as Mary after offending Mrs Harding, ending 'I wish I had just said, It's nice to meet you'. The learner sorts the polite remark from the impolite one.
Extract in which Mary mocks Mr Pomeroy's riding and shooting, and Mrs Lee reveals her brother moved here for exactly that. An impolite remark exposed.
Extract in which Mary calls the dog dirty and Mrs Harding says 'That's Towzer. It's our dog.' The blunder and its exposure.
Describe two of Mary's mistakes and their impact on the guests - the children and the bankers. Judging remarks as impolite, so 28275.
Mary's mistake about Mrs Harding's children and the awkwardness it caused. An impolite remark, not Mrs Shaw's preparations.
What Mary says when the guests try to leave - 'Oh, must you stay? Can't you go?', the opposite of the polite form she was taught.
How Mary insults the guests' hobbies - mocking horse riding, shooting and dogs. Recognising statements that fail to be polite.
